history_of_present_illness: The patient complained of recurrent fever for 3 days, with a temperature up to 39.8°C (103.6°F) the day before presentation, along with headache and diarrhoea.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient travelled to Mozambique (April 16-30) and Chile (April 30-May 17), did not take malaria chemoprophylaxis, self-treated for presumed malaria, and reported freshwater contact in a small lake near Maputo.
physical_exam: Normal physical examination with no rash, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, or lymphadenopathy.
labs_and_diagnostics: Initial labs showed eosinophilia, elevated LDH, AST/GOT, ALT/GPT, GGT, and C-reactive protein. ECG was normal, and chest radiography revealed bilateral nodular lesions in the lower lung zones, confirmed by CT scan.
differential_diagnosis: Malaria, typhoid fever, amoebic liver abscess, viral hepatitis (including hepatitis E), EBV and CMV infections, leptospirosis, rickettsioses, Q-fever, brucellosis, secondary syphilis, relapsing fever, helminth infection, acute schistosomiasis (Katayama syndrome), and acute fascioliasis.
management_and_clinical_course: Initial thick films and stool/urine microscopy for Schistosoma eggs were negative. Antischistosomal antibodies were initially negative but became positive four weeks later (IFA 1:1280, cercarial- and egg-ELISA positive); S. mansoni ova were found in the stool, and the patient was treated with praziquantel.
